title: 2012 HMMT November Team Problem 4
statement: Let \(\pi\) be a permutation of the numbers from 2 through 2012. Find the largest possible value of \(\log _{2} \pi(2) \cdot \log _{3} \pi(3) \cdots \log _{2012} \pi(2012)\).

solutions.text:
1 Note that

\[\begin{aligned}
\prod_{i=2}^{2012} \log _{i} \pi(i) & =\prod_{i=2}^{2012} \frac{\log \pi(i)}{\log i} \\
& =\frac{\prod_{i=2}^{2012} \log \pi(i)}{\prod_{i=2}^{2012} \log i} \\
& =1
\end{aligned}\]

where the last equality holds since \(\pi\) is a permutation of the numbers 2 through 2012 .
